correctness.rationale: The resolvent eigenprojector identity gives exactly two offdiagonal entry values a and b with ratio strictly in (0,1). Rademacher fourth moments reduce every partition to E=S^2-(1-r^2)Q. Even q follows from Q<=qm^2 and S^2>=0; for odd q fixed-sum convex extremality and the |S|>m comparison exclude all other minimizers, including integer-parity boundaries. Substitution gives the exact minimum and positive whole-part penalty. The independent standard-library rational verifier passed 109166 checks covering explicit inverses, all class-count assignments on small graphs and formulas. Finite tests supplement, not substitute for, the universal proof.

value.rationale: A fixed budget of two stochastic solves on a non-bipartite q-part graph makes the standard graph-coloring prescription infeasible, so determining the variance-optimal permitted two-color partition is a natural design problem. The theorem solves all balanced complete multipartite sizes and positive shifts, including every optimizer. For odd q it gives an exact strictly positive variance gain by splitting exactly one part, an explicit obstruction to any whole-part grouping. K_{2,2,2} at mu=1 saves exactly 4/37 of whole-part-only variance. The result is an analytic benchmark and not claimed as a runtime algorithm for these easy-to-diagonalize graphs.
